$comment: THE TWIN REGISTER — every capability whose logic has been COLLAPSED into an
@ai-matrx/* package. A local definition of one of these names in this repo is a
re-grown twin: the exact failure the client-package campaign exists to kill
(Arman: 'the logic of the packages is NEVER duplicated outside of the package').
Add a row the same session you delete a twin. Never add an allowlist entry to
silence a NEW twin — an allowlist entry is only for a definition that is
PROVABLY not the same capability, and it must say why in `reason`.

A WRAPPER is not a twin: a local function that BINDS the package function's options (unit, style, fallback) and delegates in a line or two is the sanctioned adapter, and needs no entry. A re-implemented BODY is a twin, always.

twins.name: isUuidShape
twins.why: The LAX UUID-shape predicate ('id or slug?'). It moved out of @ai-matrx/associations/core into kit on 2026-09-07 (associations 0.8.0, C28) so a Next.js route handler could reach it without the association store. Four host copies were deleted 2026-09-07; two host re-export doors (features/scopes/{service/associationGuards,utils/slugify}) alias it as `isUuid` for ~20 historical callers.

twins.name: uniqueChannelTopic
twins.why: Realtime channel topic minter. The host copy's module-level counter could hand out the same 'unique' topic twice across dual ESM/CJS graphs (data 0.6.3).

twins.name: isOwnEcho
twins.why: Echo suppression. The notes middleware's ~60-line isOwnEcho (monotonic updated_at + equal-timestamp content match + same-actor-while-saving) was deleted in the 2026-09-07 adoption; manager.ledger.classify covers every leg. NOTE: features/files/redux/request-ledger.ts is a DIFFERENT mechanism (a server-stamped metadata.request_id under a documented wire contract) and is allowed.

allow.reason: A DIFFERENT capability: correlation on metadata.request_id, an end-to-end write id the Python backend stamps under common-docs systems/media/file-service/WIRE_CONTRACT.md. The package's ledger infers from (table, id, updated_at, fingerprint) and has no equivalent.
Consumer of the request-id ledger above, on top of everything the package does.

twins.name: scheduleReconnect
twins.why: Reconnect backoff. Four hand-rolled ladders (notes, marketing crawl activity, vision-interview room, transcript-studio) were deleted in the 2026-09-07 adoption; the package owns jittered backoff with the 30s stability reset.

twins.name: BACKOFF_RESET_AFTER_MS
twins.why: The stability-reset constant. Resetting the attempt counter on SUBSCRIBED lets a flapping channel cycle at the 1s floor forever, firing a full catch-up each time — the package encodes the 30s rule once.

twins.name: formatDurationMs
twins.why: THE UNIT LAW: the fleet's ~35 duration twins variously took milliseconds, seconds and minutes behind an identical `formatDuration(n)` signature, so kit ships formatDurationMs / formatDurationSeconds / formatDurationMinutes and NO bare `formatDuration`. Two host copies had already re-grown under this exact name (observational-memory format.ts, marketing crawl-session-panels.tsx) and were deleted 2026-09-07. A local `formatDuration` that BINDS unit+style+fallback and delegates is an adapter, not a twin; a local `formatDurationMs` is always a twin.

twins.name: formatRelativeTime
twins.why: THE relative-timestamp formatter, unified 2026-09-07 from @ai-matrx/associations (the Intl voice) and @ai-matrx/diff (the dense '2m ago' voice) plus twelve matrx-frontend copies. Three styles behind one body: short / long / intl, plus fallback and fallbackToInput.

allow.reason: A WRAPPER over the package formatter, not a reimplementation: it binds fallback:"Never", which is this roster's own statement ("no activity on record") and not the same as an em-dash. The body is one delegating line.

twins.name: parseTimestamp
twins.why: The Postgres correction: a zone-less `timestamp without time zone` is UTC, not the viewer's local time — the classic 'times are off by N hours' bug. It lived in @ai-matrx/diff and in matrx-frontend's utils/datetime.ts as byte-level twins until 2026-09-07.

allow.reason: A WRAPPER over the package parser that adds this app's dev-time loud recovery (an unparseable value warns once in development instead of silently rendering an em-dash forever). App policy, not parsing logic; the body delegates in one line.

twins.name: formatAbsoluteDate
twins.why: Rides parseTimestamp. Collapsed 2026-09-07.

twins.name: formatFileSize
twins.why: THE byte-size formatter. It was hiding inside @ai-matrx/media's UploadProgressList React component, so six matrx-frontend twins could only reach it by depending on the media React bundle to print a byte count. Moved to kit 2026-09-07 with the display decisions written down (binary units, short labels, one decimal below ten in a unit, whole bytes below 1 KB, em-dash for unknown/negative — NEVER a confident '0 B'). 2026-09-11: the name lane read GREEN while 134 byte-size bodies lived in 67 files under OTHER names — this row now also carries the SHAPE rule below, which is what actually closed the class.
twins.shapeWhy: A byte count becoming a unit string is this capability whatever it is called. The 2026-09-07 census predicted this gap ('the census method needs a shape pass') and the 2026-09-11 re-verification proved it: formatBytes, fmtBytes, humanSize, bytesHuman, formatSize, and ~60 bare inline JSX expressions that are not definitions at all and can never be caught by a name. Pattern and its proof: scripts/byte-size-shape.mjs. A capacity constant (80 * 1024 * 1024) can never match — the rule requires a DIVISION or THRESHOLD COMPARISON against 1024, and this repo has ~60 legitimate byte ceilings that must stay untouched.

shapeAllow.reason: NOT a display formatter: gbToBytes/bytesToGb convert between a storage-quota NUMBER and the bare number an admin types into a GB form field. There is no unit label and no rounding decision — the string is parsed back into a number on submit, so kit's '1.5 GB' would break the field. The same file's display door on line 27 IS the package (export const formatBytes = formatFileSize).

twins.name: extractErrorMessage
twins.why: THE caught-value-to-string extractor (PostgrestError, axios, and a FastAPI `detail` body — a string, or an object carrying `message`). Two host bodies were deleted 2026-09-11. utils/errors.ts held a near-byte copy of the package's, which meant the 2026-08-31 FastAPI `detail` fix had to be written TWICE, and it had already fallen behind on the package's nested-error lookup and its `fallback` parameter; it is now a one-line re-export door so this repo's ~100 `@/utils/errors` importers keep their path. features/agent-shortcuts/components/ShortcutForm.tsx held a STALE copy with no `detail` branch at all, so a server refusal that said exactly why was flattened into the caller's generic fallback on that form.

twins.name: getInitials
twins.why: THE avatar initials formatter, duplicated between @ai-matrx/meet and @ai-matrx/messaging and in six matrx-frontend surfaces. Recorded display decision: a multi-part name takes FIRST + LAST ('Ana Maria Rivera' is AR); the six host copies printed AM.

allow.reason: NOT YET COLLAPSED, and not a claim that it should not be: a concurrent messaging/DM lane owns every file under features/messaging on 2026-09-07 and this one must not be touched from two sessions at once. Tracked in the census as the one open getInitials row; delete this entry when that lane lands.

twins.name: avatarPaletteIndex
twins.why: The deterministic avatar tint, byte-identical in @ai-matrx/meet and @ai-matrx/messaging. A random colour per render is a surprisingly loud bug, so there is exactly one hash.

twins.name: escapeHtml
twins.why: TEN copies were live across the fleet and THEY DID NOT ESCAPE THE SAME CHARACTERS — three did & < > only, two added ", four added ' (two as ', two as '), and a tenth wore the name escapeHtmlAttr while escaping only & < " into an HTML ATTRIBUTE. A string safe through one was an attribute break-out through another. kit ships ONE decided set: & < > " ' — all five, always. It is not in @ai-matrx/print because an HTML escaper must not require jspdf + html2canvas.

twins.name: Accordion
twins.why: The Accordion family (design-system 0.8.0, census row 19c). The fork at components/ui/accordion.tsx was the fleet's only real implementation — workflow-studio's DB-authored scope was standing four bare <div>s in for it. Three fork defects died with it: a chevron-rotation selector that matched any icon passed as a direct trigger child instead of the chevron, a trigger with no focus-visible ring, and an open/close transition built on animate-accordion-down/-up — host-only Tailwind utilities, now package-owned .matrx-accordion-content CSS. Density is the `size` prop; the host binds nothing because its fork drew the package default (md).

twins.name: _registerHost
twins.why: The opener HOST REGISTRY. Four hand-rolled copies existed (kit's confirm plus this repo's sandbox-gate, scope-mismatch and value-prompts dialogs); the three host-side ones kept the registry in a module-level `let host`, which is the dual-loader-graph hazard — with unsplit dual ESM/CJS bundles each graph instantiates its own module, so host registration silently splits from its callers and the awaiting promise hangs forever with no error anywhere. Deleted here 2026-09-11 in the kit 0.10.0 adoption; `createOpener(slot)` owns the registry, the queue and the globalThis slot.

twins.name: _unregisterHost
twins.why: The unregister half of the opener host registry, including the rule that only the CURRENT host may unregister (a superseded host's late unmount must not tear down the live one — the React double-mount / provider-swap case). Deleted here 2026-09-11 alongside _registerHost.

twins.name: useOpenerHost
twins.why: The MOUNT-SIDE machinery of an imperative dialog host: registration, the ref-backed request queue, the tick-driven drain effect and the settle-once callback. Every dialog host in this repo was re-writing the same twenty lines, each with its own chance at the stale-`active`-closure bug that drops the second queued request forever. A host component that declares its own queueRef/tick/drain effect is this twin re-grown.
